reasoning:
The reproduction re-runs and produces the stated numbers (237/410 = 57.8%). The CODE claim is also true: src/api/data_contract.py:3060-3068 takes plain arithmetic means of ordinals with no normalization. But the INFERENTIAL STEP fails, and with it the P0 story.

(1) rawRank / pool-size is not a valid ground truth, so 'flips under it' does not mean 'is wrong'. dlfSf (278 rows) and ktcSfTep (499 rows) rank NESTED SUBSETS of the same universe in the same order. Two boards that agree perfectly give a player the SAME ordinal; dividing by 278 vs 499 manufactures a 0.24-percentile 'disagreement' out of exact agreement. The finding's proposed repair ('normalise both sides by each source's own pool size, reusing the map _percentile_rank_spread builds') would therefore INTRODUCE error on the 12 pure-offense boards, not remove it. _percentile_rank_spread needs pool sizes because it measures max-minus-min across sources whose ladder-translated EFFECTIVE ranks live in different spaces; _compute_market_gap is handed raw same-space ordinals for 19 of 21 sources. The two functions are not the same problem and the docstring the finding quotes does not indict this one.

(2) The real incommensurability is asset-class COMPOSITION, not depth. Measured on the live contract: ktcSfTep = 463 OFF + 36 PICK; idpTradeCalc = 437 OFF + 370 IDP + 96 PICK; every other offense source is 100% OFF. So KTC's offense ordinals are inflated ~30 by interleaved picks and IDPTC's by ~190 by interleaved defenders — and those two biases push in OPPOSITE directions.

(3) Correcting for that (re-densify each source's ordinal within the row's own asset class, no percentile at all) the stamped direction survives on 335/386 offense rows and 23/24 pick rows. The finding's headline pick number (23/24 = 95.8% flip) collapses to 1/24 — it was almost entirely an artifact of dividing pick ranks by each source's whole-board pool. Only 8 offense rows carry a RENDERED /rankings badge opposite to the population-matched direction, and 7 of the 8 have a true gap under 5.2 ranks, i.e. arbitrary near-ties. Exactly ONE row (Elijah Moore, consensus rank 654) is both rendered and materially wrong. On /trade, where MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP is 3, 34 rows flip and 16 are material.

(4) The P0 anchor is simply wrong. Calvin Ridley: KTC raw 325 is rank 295 once KTC's 36 picks are removed from its own board; the population-matched consensus mean is 253.1. Consensus really does rank him ~42 ranks better than retail. 'consensus_premium' -> BUY is the CORRECT label. There is no user acting on a wrong number for the named player, so the P0 predicate is unmet.

(5) Sub-claim 'the EDGE column is permanently blank for 40% of the board ... the column has no coverage note' is false. /rankings renders marketAction(row) (frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1165-1172), which for an IDP row returns label '-' with title 'No KTC rank for this player - only expert/consensus sources contributed.' (display-helpers.js:139-146, 231-236). A per-row explanation IS shown on hover. The 293-IDP 'none' census does reproduce.

(6) Blast radius recount: claimed 237 players affected. Real: 8 rows whose /rankings badge is opposite (1 material) and 34 rows whose /trade BUY/SELL is opposite (16 material). A ~30x overstatement.

Rescoped defect that DOES survive: _compute_market_gap averages ordinals across sources with different asset-class composition without re-densifying within the row's class, so KTC's 36 interleaved picks and idpTradeCalc's 370 interleaved defenders both bias the comparison. Repair is to re-densify each source's rank within the row's asset class before differencing - NOT to divide by pool size.
whatWouldSettleIt: A ground-truth definition of 'the same population'. My population-matched recount assumes each source's rank list within an asset class is a nested subset of one universe. Publishing per-source, per-asset-class dense ranks in sourceRankMeta (the pipeline already stamps rawRank and a fixed-N percentile) would let the direction be computed unambiguously and the residual 51-row disagreement adjudicated row by row.

reasoning:
The reproduction runs verbatim and every number in it is right, and I strengthened it: the finding asserts the 18 extra sources come from today's tree but never proved they are absent from the snapshot. They are - the archive's _canonicalSiteValues carries exactly three keys across all 1,074 players (idpTradeCalc 814, ktc 464, ktcSfTep 464), so the other 18 voters can only have come from CSVs/site_raw/ at the paths hardcoded at data_contract.py:279-470. pfkDynasty.csv and fantasyNavigatorSf.csv were first ADDED to the tree on 2026-08-03; they could not have contributed to any board served on 2026-07-14, yet they vote in its 'replay'. That is an airtight temporal leak, and all three cited backtest scripts do exactly this (backtest_alpha_shrinkage.py:71, backtest_soft_fallback.py:69, backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py:118-121 all call build_api_data_contract on a loaded snapshot). The reports and the player_valuation.py 'served board' comment exist as quoted (reports/*.md:3 'Snapshot count: 25'; src/canonical/player_valuation.py:71-76).

What I am rescoping is the SCOPE and SEVERITY, both of which are inflated to the point of being unusable.

(1) blastRadius {playersAffected 1092, routesAffected 100, pagesAffected 38} is a category error. It counts the entire site because the value model is unvalidated. No route serves a backtest; no page renders one; not one number a user sees changes if every report in reports/ is deleted. The artifacts actually affected are 7 files in reports/, 3 scripts in scripts/, 2 source comments, and the tuning PROVENANCE of alpha=0.10 / lambda / _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N. Severity without an honest blastRadius is rejected by the protocol's own rule 4, and this one would survive merge as '100 routes affected'.

(2) The strongest single instance the finding cites is the weakest one in impact. The player_valuation.py 'served board' comment sits directly under a header (lines 55-58) reading 'RECONSTRUCTION-ONLY. Nothing on the live valuation path evaluates these' - HILL_MIDPOINT/HILL_SLOPE are not live constants. And the primary fit that comment describes IS against a served board: backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py defaults to exports/latest and rebuilds it with today's CSVs on the same day, which reproduces what was served. Only the trailing '16 archived snapshots spanning 07-16 -> 07-30' STABILITY claim is a counterfactual. So 'the word served is false' is true of one clause, not of the sentence.

(3) Where the leak does bite is alpha-shrinkage / MAD-lambda / percentile-reference-N, which ARE live constants, and there the finding's real point is sharper than it states it: with 18 of 21 sources frozen at today's values across every 'snapshot', consecutive-day deltas are driven almost entirely by the 3 sources that ARE archived, so a stability result is close to guaranteed by construction. The conclusion that these reports cannot support a tuning decision follows. The conclusion that 'NO model in this repository may be described as validated' does not - the finding's own whatWorks concedes src/model_registry/board_holdout.py scores against realized 2025 points, and per CLAUDE.md that is the path the promotion gate actually runs on.

(4) Priority: P1 is not defensible for a defect with zero user-facing surface. Nobody acts on a wrong number; the served board may be entirely correct. This is a validation-integrity and documentation defect - real, worth fixing, and correctly scoped as P2. The requiredRepair (write playersArray into exports, archive all 21 CSVs per snapshot, give build_api_data_contract an optional site_raw root) is sound and I would keep it verbatim, including the last line - no backtest in reports/ should be cited as evidence until it lands.
whatWouldSettleIt: One export written with playersArray embedded, replayed through a build_api_data_contract given a site_raw root pointing at that snapshot's own CSVs: if the replayed rankDerivedValue matches the embedded one row for row, the leak is closed and the backtests become citable. Nothing available in this container can do that today because no such export exists.
